heroHeadline: GSMA: Africa's 63% Usage Gap Is a Skills Crisis; Kenya and ITU Launch Five-Country AI Youth Programme
heroSubtitle: GSMA Mobile Economy 2026 data reveals that 63% of Africans with mobile coverage still don't use the internet — the world's highest usage gap — driven by digital skills deficits rather than infrastructure absence. On May 12, Kenya and the ITU launched a national AI and robotics youth programme, part of a five-country initiative (Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa) targeting the skills barrier in the continent's largest digital economies. Separately, Starlink's constellation reached 11,979 total satellites with active service in 166 countries, and Starlink plus Amazon Leo are positioned for a combined ~$1B allocation from the US BEAD broadband program as the administration shifts toward satellite-first rural connectivity.
footerNote: Data sourced from ITU, GSMA, World Bank, A4AI, SpaceX regulatory filings, Amazon, FCC, and major international research outlets. Contested figures noted with confidence levels.
